assessments.reasoning: The exact Microsoft-authored reference as transcribed in PCjs identifies QuickBASIC 4.5 as a programming language. Its Introduction identifies a companion book for learning the development environment.

challenge.method: Compare the fixed MSPL text with its rendered edition, the independently archived CD topic indexes, and the original release-media documentation and Microsoft KnowledgeBase articles. Test whether the claimed identity requires treating the transcription itself as an original print or disk image.
challenge.results: The Microsoft title, separate reference and environment publications, and release evidence support the adopted source role for a documented-source claim whose representation is explicitly identified as a transcription. A related disk archive and indexes corroborate provenance without establishing a byte-for-byte edition reconstruction of the complete reference text.

limitations: The claim describes the scope of the language reference. The exact relied-on bytes are the pinned transcription, and no original Microsoft execution was performed.
